# iTunesDB golden fixtures

`original-empty.b64` is the Base64 representation of a 3,508-byte iTunesDB
generated by the Original iOpenPod `write_mhbd` implementation with no tracks,
fixed database and master-playlist IDs, Unix time 1,700,000,000, and random seed 0.
It was imported on 2026-08-27 as the local compatibility baseline described by
ADR-0004.

Decoded SHA-256:
`23576f070e32bd561f803724a98606ed8ce95543b30917819565031b57bff33b`.

The encoded text form keeps the fixture reviewable and platform-neutral. Tests
decode it strictly before asserting complete byte equality.

## Captured album index, sort type 36

`captured-album-index-36.b64` is a reduced 194,202-byte fixture derived from the
historical 20,138,994-byte captured database. It contains 60 Tracks across nine
complete native albums, their album records, and both Master Playlists. Retained
Track/album Chunks originate in that capture. Unselected Tracks, albums, ordinary
Playlists, other datasets, and other browse indexes are removed. Master occurrences
are filtered in their original order; the original sort-36 sequences are filtered
and remapped to those reduced occurrence positions. Structural lengths/counts are
recalculated, and a fresh unsigned root is used. This is not a publishable device
backup and makes no claim about absent artwork or media.

`captured-album-index-36.json` records the source and fixture SHA-256 hashes, source
Track IDs, and expected ordered Track IDs read from the original MHOD 52 records.
Those expected sequences are not generated by the index implementation under test.
The database alone supplies the test evidence, without a runtime dependency on
Original iOpenPod or the user's capture folder.

See [sort-36 research](../../../docs/research/itunesdb-sort-36.md) for the observed
rules and evidence limits.
